title: The Last Crown Again
premise: Edmund Winterbourne steals memories for coin, wiping the minds of the desperate and selling their pasts to collectors in the city of Vael. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Edmund discovers it charts the resting place of the Last Crown — an artifact of the Thornfell kings that can either bind the mountain's ancient magic or unleash a war thought buried for three centuries. Hunted by the Crown's old loyalists and the empire that fears its return, Edmund must decide whether to sell the secret, destroy it, or claim it himself. In the end he shatters the Crown beneath the mountains, losing his own stolen memories to do so, and chooses an unwritten future over an inherited one.
about_author: Lior Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city before turning to fiction. They write about inheritance, memory, and the lies families tell to survive.

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Yesterdays
chapters.summary: Edmund lifts a merchant's grief from her mind in a Vael back-alley, then sells it to a collector who pays too well. POV: Edmund. Establishes his trade's moral rot and his own hollowed-out past. Emotional beat: quiet self-disgust masked as professionalism.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: A wounded courier collapses into Edmund's rented room, pursued by riders in imperial grey. With his last breath the man presses a leather map case into Edmund's hands and whispers a name: 'Thornfell keeps.' POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: panic and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Edmund studies the map, which resists his memory-stealing touch — the first thing he cannot take. Imperial soldiers ransack the district; he flees through smuggler roads only he knows. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: hunted adrenaline, first taste of being the stolen rather than the thief.

chapters.title: The Road Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Edmund travels the mountain passes toward the map's first marker, guided by childhood knowledge he'd rather forget. He encounters a burned village and realizes others are searching too. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: dread deepening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sera of the Ash Choir
chapters.summary: Edmund is ambushed by Sera, a survivor of the burned village and sworn member of the Ash Choir, loyalists guarding the Crown's secret. She spares him when she sees the map. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into vigilance; wary alliance begins.

chapters.title: The Choir's Bargain
chapters.summary: The Ash Choir's leader, Mother Ivenna, offers Edmund protection if he carries the map to the Crown's vault — but admits she intends to use the Crown to restore the old kingdom. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: suspicion; he realizes allies may be another kind of cage.

chapters.title: Memories He Never Sold
chapters.summary: Resting in the Choir's hidden hold, Edmund is haunted by fragments of his own erased childhood — Thornfell, a burning tower, a woman's voice. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: vertigo; the thief discovers he was robbed first.

chapters.title: The Grey Company
chapters.summary: Imperial inquisitor Captain Rell captures two Choir scouts and interrogates them with a memory-extraction engine. Through a scout's eyes we learn the empire fears the Crown because it once broke their founding emperor. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: cold conviction; the antagonist believes he is merciful.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Hold
chapters.summary: A Choir traitor sells the route to Rell. The hold burns; Mother Ivenna dies buying Edmund and Sera time to escape with the map. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: fury and guilt — survival again purchased with someone else's life.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: On the run above the snowline, Sera confronts Edmund: everyone near him dies. He confesses his memory-trade and his erased past. POV: alternating Edmund/Sera. Emotional beat: raw honesty; loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: The Collector's Offer
chapters.summary: Master Corvane, the collector from chapter one, finds Edmund with an offer: deliver the map, and receive the memories stolen from him as a child — his whole identity restored. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation crystallized; the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Who Was Edmund Winterbourne
chapters.summary: Corvane reveals a fragment free of charge: Edmund is the last heir of the Thornfell line, his memories taken to hide him. The Crown will answer to his blood alone. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: identity collapse; every choice reframed.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera learns the truth and must choose between the Choir's mission, her vengeance on the empire, and the man she's begun to trust. She stays — but no longer blindly. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: love and loyalty re-forged on harder terms.

chapters.title: Descent at the Weeping Gate
chapters.summary: Guided by the map, they enter the Weeping Gate caverns beneath Thornfell's peak, evading Rell's trackers through flooded galleries and singing stone. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: awe and claustrophobia; the past literally closing around them.

chapters.title: The Vault of Kings
chapters.summary: They reach the vault and find the Last Crown — alive, humming, showing Edmund visions of every king who wore it and what it cost them. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: terrible recognition; the Crown's power is memory itself.

chapters.title: Rell at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Rell and the Grey Company breach the vault. He offers Edmund clemency if the Crown is destroyed — but his engine will also erase every mind in the valley, including the refugees sheltering there. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: the antagonist's mercy revealed as annihilation.

chapters.title: Crown of Thorns, Crown of Memory
chapters.summary: Cornered, Edmund takes up the Crown. It floods him with the full history of Thornfell — including proof that his family erased themselves willingly to end the last war. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: transcendence and horror fused.

chapters.title: The Breaking
chapters.summary: Climax: Edmund refuses both Corvane's restoration and Rell's erasure. Wearing the Crown, he unbinds its power into the mountain itself, shattering it — paying with every stolen memory he ever kept, including his own name. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: sacrificial clarity.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: Rell, his engine dead and his certainty broken, withdraws — changed. Corvane flees empty-handed. The mountain goes quiet for the first time in centuries. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: exhausted relief shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: A Man Without Yesterdays
chapters.summary: Edmund wakes remembering almost nothing. Sera tells him who he was and what he chose, giving him back his story piece by piece — the one inheritance freely given. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road, Southward
chapters.summary: Edmund and Sera leave Thornfell together, walking roads he no longer knows, choosing to learn them anew rather than reclaim them. Rumors stir that other crowns sleep elsewhere. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: cautious hope; freedom as beginning, not ending.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What Survives Us
chapters.summary: In Vael, a child finds one of Edmund's discarded memory-vials and hears a stranger's laughter inside it. Somewhere, Edmund laughs the same way without knowing why. POV: omniscient. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure — memory outlives its keepers.
